messages:
leo: Alert from the backup-integrity job: found 37 object parts in `gs://redwood-backups/tenant-77/2026-04-02/` that lack `x-goog-server-side-encryption` metadata.

anya: whoa. are these whole objects or multipart upload parts?

leo: looks like multipart parts. filenames end with `.part-0N` and size < 5MB in many cases. backup-agent retries create a single-part upload on small chunks.

mike: did any RBAC or uploader role changes happen yesterday? i remember an oncall tweak to the backup serviceaccount at 23:45 UTC.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: backup-agent/2.14.1 -> 2.14.2 @2026-04-01T23:50:00Z by mike (rev d2c9).

leo: that matches. diff shows a small retry handler change to `multipart_replay()` that skips SSE headers when reusing a cached presigned URL.

anya: are these objects actually unencrypted on GCS or just missing metadata? gcloud `object.get` can show `kmsKeyName` and `customerEncryption` fields.

leo: quick check: `gsutil stat gs://redwood-backups/.../part-001` returns no `KMSKeyName` and `Encryption` block empty. seems stored plaintext in bucket. urgent.

sec-bot: SENSITIVITY SCAN: 3 objects match pattern `*tenant-77*password*` — flagged, data-at-rest exposure high.

mike: we need to triage scope. did the uploader ever use CMEK for the bucket or rely on per-object SSE-C? we have both historically.

leo: bucket default KMS is `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/backup/cryptoKeys/backup-cmek` — but object-level key absent for these parts. so CMEK wasn't applied for them.

anya: immediate containment: restrict access to that prefix (bucket IAM object-level deny for all roles except backup-recover-role) and add a short-lived ACL to prevent public-read. can ops do that now?

mike: on it. applying object-level restriction via gsutil iam ch on prefix.

gcs-ci: permission update: denied write/list to `allUsers` and removed `projectViewer` access on `gs://redwood-backups/tenant-77/2026-04-02/` at 2026-04-02T00:04:12Z.

leo: thanks. question: how did plaintext end up in bucket if backup-agent normally encrypts before upload? possibility: agent switched to client-side encrypt then uploaded parts without completing envelope step. or presigned URL path bypassed client encryption.

anya: check KMS audit logs for Encrypt/GenerateDataKey calls from backup-agent around 23:45-00:00. if we see no GenerateDataKey then agent skipped envelope encryption.

leo: i'm running a Cloud Audit Log filter: `resource.type=cloudkms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName=GenerateRandomBytes OR Encrypt`.

leo: quick result: no GenerateDataKey/Encrypt entries from serviceaccount `service-backup@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` between 2026-04-01T23:45 and 2026-04-02T00:05. other keys show activity though.

mike: that implies agent didn't call KMS. could RBAC change have removed `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt` permission on the agent SA? check iam policy delta.

deploy-bot: iam-change: removed `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` binding from `service-backup@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` at 2026-04-01T23:46 by infra-admin (chore-789).

anya: that would explain it. but deploy diff indicated code change too. we have two contributing failures: RBAC removal + retry bug = plaintext parts. not good.

leo: action list proposed: 1) incident open + notify legal/compliance, 2) rotate backup CMEK (create new key version), 3) re-upload missing parts encrypted (if possible) or mark snapshot as compromised, 4) revert RBAC removal for backup agent and add a gated change, 5) add CI test to fail deployment if KMS permissions removed for backup SA.

sec-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - INC-2026-0402-09 - severity: high (potential cleartext backup). Owner: eng-security.

mike: rotating CMEK now and giving backup SA back encrypter role.

mike: iam patch applied: restored `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to service-backup@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 2026-04-02T00:10:02Z.

leo: good. next: can we determine whether any of the 37 parts were downloaded externally before lock-down? check object access logs / requester logs.

anya: enabling Object Access Logging (ACL logs) retroactively won't show past GETs unless audit log already recorded them. check Cloud Storage access logs in audit logs.

leo: search shows no external requester principals, only internal uploader/proxy. doesn't rule out compromise but lowers immediate risk.

mike: for the snapshot itself we should err on safe side: mark as compromised and schedule customer-facing remediation if tenant data included sensitive fields. legal to advise.

anya: vuln triage notes: root cause = RBAC drift + insufficient deployment guard + backup-agent multipart retry bug. fix plan: revert RBAC drift (done), patch agent to always attach kms metadata on retries and add a preflight that calls GenerateDataKey and fails fast, and add an automated post-deploy check verifying object KMS metadata for small sample.

leo: i'll create a runbook entry for encrypted-upload smoke: `python tools/encrypt_smoke.py --target gs://... --verify --retries 3` and add it to canary runs.

sec-bot: ATTACHMENT: vuln-triage-template INC-2026-0402-09.csv posted to /tmp and security jira created SEC-847.

mike: i'll open a PR to revert the retry change and include new tests. tagging @anya for review.

anya: ack. add a follow-up to quarterly audit to scan for object-level missing CMEK across all buckets.

leo: thanks team. closing until PR lands and legal confirms communication path. :lock:
